Today’s M&A briefing — 20 deals, the strategies behind them · 13 November 2026

🔹 Danone finalizes the acquisition of Made Group (health-focused food products, Australia, over €300M revenue) — €1.2bn.

🔹 KAST acquires Gemini's European operations (cryptocurrency exchange platform, teams, licenses) — $10m.
Gemini retains only its US and Singaporean markets.

🔹 Worker.ai (enterprise operating system platform for SMEs, bringing together plans) acquires DeltaGen (real-time voice AI extracting decisions, commitments) — $1.2m.

🔹 Telia acquires Telavox's Nordic enterprise client portfolio (telavox's B2B client base in the Nordic countries).

🔹 WeRoad (italian community travel platform, over 1,000 itineraries) acquires TravelTribe (swiss brand for sports and community travel).

🔹 First Capital Partner GmbH (investment company based in Gräfelfing, Germany) acquires PATRIZIA SE (listed real estate asset manager in Augsburg).

🔹 Derichebourg Facility acquires Propreté Environnement and Services (PES) (industrial cleaning and cleaning of agri-food sites).

🔹 Vizrt (graphics and production solutions for broadcasting, Norway) acquires Chyron (titling systems and graphics for digital broadcasting, United States).

🔹 Autentic (audiovisual production and distribution, Germany) acquires Gedeon Media Group (GMG) assets (factual documentary production, France).
Following the acquisition, Autentic launches Gedeon Studios.

🔹 DX (british logistics operator, national B2B and B2C delivery network) acquires Fulfil with Synergy (FwS) (multichannel fulfillment and retail distribution from Northampton).

🔹 Nordex Group (german wind turbine manufacturer) signs an acquisition agreement for C1 Connections (onshore wind turbine tower connection engineering).

🔹 Maco Gruppe (austrian manufacturer of fittings for windows, doors) takes a majority stake in ekey biometric systems GmbH (biometric and digital access solutions).

🔹 Sacmi Imola / Protesa takes a majority stake in S.T (failure analysis, testing, and quality control).

🔹 Lego Digital Play acquires ForthStar Games (mobile game studio based in Manchester, founded).

🔹 Unica acquires Wassink Installatie (design, execution, and maintenance of technical installations, HVAC).

🔹 QNP / Techone (dutch ICT group majority-owned by KKR since late 2025) acquires Aucuba Automatisering (IT services for SMEs, Breda, over twenty-five years of experience).

🔹 Ondernemersadviseurs (business consulting) acquires Pure Minds (digital marketing agency, Kerkrade, Netherlands).

➕ 3 more deals in the carousel.

en.text:
Today’s fundraising briefing — 7 deals, the strategies behind them · 13 November 2026

🔹 Uforce (autonomous defense drones, United Kingdom) — $700m · Series A.
𝗜𝗻𝘃𝗲𝘀𝘁𝗼𝗿𝘀: UK National Wealth Fund, co-lead.
𝗢𝘂𝗿 𝘃𝗶𝗲𝘄: The presence of the UK National Wealth Fund as co-lead signals that the British government considers sovereignty in military drones as national infrastructure to be directly funded.

🔹 Agile Robots (humanoid robots and AI-powered automated arms for automotive, electronics, healthcare, and services, Munich, founded in 2018) — €450m.
The funding round brings Agile Robots' valuation to approximately €7.6B, the first valuation in robotics and AI in Europe according to the company. German automakers are cited as early adopters of humanoid solutions as early as 2027.
𝗨𝘀𝗲 𝗼𝗳 𝗳𝘂𝗻𝗱𝘀: Expansion in the United States, increased production capacity in Germany, entry into new markets.
𝗜𝗻𝘃𝗲𝘀𝘁𝗼𝗿𝘀: SoftBank; Nvidia; Hitachi; T.Capital (Deutsche Telekom's investment vehicle).
𝗢𝘂𝗿 𝘃𝗶𝗲𝘄: Nvidia and SoftBank are not just buying a stake: they are funding an outlet for their own infrastructure — each deployed humanoid is a compute unit sold for Nvidia, a structuring portfolio axis for SoftBank.

🔹 SE3 (AI software for 3D spatial understanding of drones and unmanned military systems) — $30m · Series A.
Founded by Lukas Köstler (formerly Tesla Autopilot and Nvidia Research), SE3 has contracts with the Bundeswehr and is deploying its technology in Ukraine. The Series A comes less than five months after exiting stealth mode with €5.5M in seed funding.
𝗢𝘂𝗿 𝘃𝗶𝗲𝘄: The choice of classic computer vision algorithms to distill sensor data, rather than large generalist models, reflects military engineering discipline: reliability takes precedence over flexibility in a cluttered environment.

🔹 Nebuly (platform for measuring AI agent ROI for large enterprises, connected to Claude, ChatGPT, and Microsoft Copilot, Turin and New York) — €18.95m · Series A.
The platform measures internal efficiency gains (hours saved, capacity freed up) and customer impacts (influenced revenue, churn risks, upsell opportunities). It can be deployed on-premise or in a private cloud.

🔹 ValkaAI (real-time generative AI for digital characters reacting with speech, expressions, and movements to live events) — €13m · Pre-seed.
Founded by Vlastimil Venclík (founder of Oddin.gg) and Miloš Lokajíček, ValkaAI employs approximately 50 people, including researchers from Meta and DeepMind.
𝗨𝘀𝗲 𝗼𝗳 𝗳𝘂𝗻𝗱𝘀: Research in real-time video and audio generation, recruitment of senior researchers, business development.

🔹 MISTT — £5m · Pre-seed.

🔹 well raises €3.6 million in pre-seed funding — €3.6m.

Levées de fonds : les 7 opérations chiffrées de l'édito du 13 novembre 2026.

🔹 Uforce (𝑑𝑟𝑜𝑛𝑒𝑠 𝑑𝑒 𝑑𝑒́𝑓𝑒𝑛𝑠𝑒 𝑎𝑢𝑡𝑜𝑛𝑜𝑚𝑒𝑠, 𝑅𝑜𝑦𝑎𝑢𝑚𝑒-𝑈𝑛𝑖) — 700 M$ · Série A.
𝗔𝘃𝗲𝗰 : UK National Wealth Fund, co-chef de file.
𝗣𝗼𝗶𝗻𝘁 𝗱𝗲 𝘃𝘂𝗲 : La présence du UK National Wealth Fund comme co-chef de file signale que le gouvernement britannique considère la souveraineté dans les drones militaires comme une infrastructure nationale à financer directement.

🔹 Agile Robots (𝑟𝑜𝑏𝑜𝑡𝑠 ℎ𝑢𝑚𝑎𝑛𝑜𝑖̈𝑑𝑒𝑠 𝑒𝑡 𝑏𝑟𝑎𝑠 𝑎𝑢𝑡𝑜𝑚𝑎𝑡𝑖𝑠𝑒́𝑠 𝑑𝑜𝑡𝑒́𝑠 𝑑'𝐼𝐴 𝑝𝑜𝑢𝑟 𝑙'𝑎𝑢𝑡𝑜𝑚𝑜𝑏𝑖𝑙𝑒, 𝑙'𝑒́𝑙𝑒𝑐𝑡𝑟𝑜𝑛𝑖𝑞𝑢𝑒, 𝑙𝑎 𝑠𝑎𝑛𝑡𝑒́ 𝑒𝑡 𝑙𝑒𝑠 𝑠𝑒𝑟𝑣𝑖𝑐𝑒𝑠, 𝑀𝑢𝑛𝑖𝑐ℎ) — 450 M€.
La levée porte la valorisation d'Agile Robots à environ 7,6 Md€, première valorisation en robotique et IA en Europe selon la société. Les constructeurs automobiles allemands sont cités comme premiers adopteurs des solutions humanoïdes dès 2027.
𝗢𝗯𝗷𝗲𝗰𝘁𝗶𝗳 : Expansion aux États-Unis, augmentation des capacités de production en Allemagne, entrée sur de nouveaux marchés.
𝗔𝘃𝗲𝗰 : SoftBank ; Nvidia ; Hitachi ; T.Capital (véhicule d'investissement de Deutsche Telekom).
𝗣𝗼𝗶𝗻𝘁 𝗱𝗲 𝘃𝘂𝗲 : Nvidia et SoftBank n'achètent pas seulement une participation : ils financent un débouché pour leur propre infrastructure — chaque humanoïde déployé est une unité de compute vendue pour Nvidia, un axe structurant de portefeuille pour SoftBank.

🔹 SE3 (𝑙𝑜𝑔𝑖𝑐𝑖𝑒𝑙𝑠 𝑑'𝐼𝐴 𝑝𝑜𝑢𝑟 𝑙𝑎 𝑐𝑜𝑚𝑝𝑟𝑒́ℎ𝑒𝑛𝑠𝑖𝑜𝑛 𝑠𝑝𝑎𝑡𝑖𝑎𝑙𝑒 3𝐷 𝑑𝑒 𝑑𝑟𝑜𝑛𝑒𝑠 𝑒𝑡 𝑠𝑦𝑠𝑡𝑒̀𝑚𝑒𝑠 𝑚𝑖𝑙𝑖𝑡𝑎𝑖𝑟𝑒𝑠 𝑠𝑎𝑛𝑠 𝑝𝑖𝑙𝑜𝑡𝑒) — 30 M$ · Série A.
Fondée par Lukas Köstler (ancien Tesla Autopilot et Nvidia Research), SE3 a des contrats avec la Bundeswehr et déploie sa technologie en Ukraine. La série A intervient moins de cinq mois après une sortie de phase confidentielle avec 5,5 M€ de seed.
𝗣𝗼𝗶𝗻𝘁 𝗱𝗲 𝘃𝘂𝗲 : Le choix d'algorithmes classiques de vision par ordinateur pour distiller les données capteurs, plutôt que de grands modèles généralistes, reflète une discipline d'ingénierie militaire : la fiabilité prime sur la flexibilité dans un environnement brouillé.

🔹 Nebuly (𝑝𝑙𝑎𝑡𝑒𝑓𝑜𝑟𝑚𝑒 𝑑𝑒 𝑚𝑒𝑠𝑢𝑟𝑒 𝑑𝑢 𝑅𝑂𝐼 𝑑𝑒𝑠 𝑎𝑔𝑒𝑛𝑡𝑠 𝐼𝐴 𝑝𝑜𝑢𝑟 𝑔𝑟𝑎𝑛𝑑𝑒𝑠 𝑒𝑛𝑡𝑟𝑒𝑝𝑟𝑖𝑠𝑒𝑠, 𝑐𝑜𝑛𝑛𝑒𝑐𝑡𝑒́𝑒 𝑎̀ 𝐶𝑙𝑎𝑢𝑑𝑒, 𝐶ℎ𝑎𝑡𝐺𝑃𝑇 𝑒𝑡 𝑀𝑖𝑐𝑟𝑜𝑠𝑜𝑓𝑡 𝐶𝑜𝑝𝑖𝑙𝑜𝑡) — 18,95 M€ · Série A.

🔹 ValkaAI (𝐼𝐴 𝑔𝑒́𝑛𝑒́𝑟𝑎𝑡𝑖𝑣𝑒 𝑒𝑛 𝑡𝑒𝑚𝑝𝑠 𝑟𝑒́𝑒𝑙 𝑝𝑜𝑢𝑟 𝑝𝑒𝑟𝑠𝑜𝑛𝑛𝑎𝑔𝑒𝑠 𝑛𝑢𝑚𝑒́𝑟𝑖𝑞𝑢𝑒𝑠 𝑟𝑒́𝑎𝑔𝑖𝑠𝑠𝑎𝑛𝑡 𝑝𝑎𝑟 𝑙𝑎 𝑝𝑎𝑟𝑜𝑙𝑒) — 13 M€ · Pré-seed.
